# CrewAI Research Pipeline Status: complete One-liner: A four-agent research system — Planner, Researcher, Writer, Critic — with LLM-as-Judge scoring and streamed intermediate output. Stack: CrewAI, ChromaDB, SSE, Python Live URL: https://research-pipeline-frontend.vercel.app Repository: https://github.com/SpandanNagale/crewai-research-pipeline ## Design rationale (why it was built this way) Splitting research into Planner, Researcher, Writer, and Critic roles keeps each agent's context narrow enough to stay reliable, and makes the failure visible when it happens — you can see which stage produced the bad output instead of debugging one long opaque generation. The Critic runs an LLM-as-Judge pass over the draft rather than the pipeline simply terminating on the Writer's first output, and SSE streaming exposes every intermediate stage to the user, which turns a black box into something inspectable. This was later extended into an Enterprise AI Research Agent for a take-home assignment. ## Anticipated questions Q: Isn't LLM-as-Judge just the same model grading itself? A: Largely, yes — that's the known weakness, and it's why the Critic here scores drafts rather than gating anything destructive. DataSleuth uses execution-based verification precisely because judgment-based verification wasn't strong enough for that use case. ## Repository facts (from GitHub) - Stars: 0 - Last commit: 2026-09-17T14:11:47Z - GitHub description: Production-ready multi-agent research API built with CrewAI + Gemma 4. Features a FastAPI backend, Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming, and an automated eval scorer for citation, coverage, and clarity. ## Languages (by bytes, from GitHub) - Python: 345321 - TypeScript: 37608 - Dockerfile: 2239 - CSS: 2062 - Mako: 704 - JavaScript: 559 ## README # Research Pipeline A multi-agent research pipeline built on **CrewAI** and pluggable Large Language Models (local **Ollama** by default — zero cost, no API key — with optional **Ollama Cloud**, **Groq**, **OpenRouter**, and **Gemini** backends). Six specialized agents plan, research, cross-check, classify, write, and critique a report on any topic; every finding, source, contradiction, conclusion, and pipeline-run event is persisted so the whole reasoning chain is traceable, resumable, and reusable. Three interfaces over one backend: 1. 🖥️ **Web dashboard** (Next.js, `frontend/`) — three panes: run configuration, the live pipeline via real-time SSE, and the finished report with inline claims/sources. 2. ⚡ **REST API** (FastAPI, `app.py`) — streaming, traceability, knowledge-search, and health endpoints. 3. ⌨️ **CLI** (`main.py`) — one-shot terminal runs. --- ## 🏗️ Architecture & Workflow An incoming topic first passes the **input guardrail** (length, gibberish, prompt-injection, role-override, code-generation, and PII checks — all heuristic, no LLM call). It's then embedded (Gemini) and compared against past `research_questions` in the vector store (Postgres+pgvector in deployment, an in-process NumPy backend for local dev — see [Knowledge reuse](#knowledge-reuse)); a close-enough match short-circuits the whole pipeline and returns the existing findings/conclusions. Otherwise the six-stage pipeline runs, persisting every stage's output to the DB as it goes — not just at the end — and streaming a `RunEvent` for each meaningful thing that happens (`observability/`) so a client can watch it live. ```mermaid graph TD User([User Topic]) --> Guard{Input guardrail} Guard -->|Blocked| Rejected[400 GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED] Guard -->|OK| Reuse{Similar question
already answered?} Reuse -->|Yes, above threshold| Existing[Return existing findings
+ conclusions from DB] Reuse -->|No| Planner[Planner] Planner -->|Sub-questions| Researcher[Researcher] Researcher -->|Atomic findings, one per source
written to sources + findings| Comparator[Evidence Comparator] Comparator -->|Contradictions written to
contradictions table| Classifier[Classifier] Classifier -->|Category written to
findings.category| Writer[Writer] Writer -->|Draft report| Critic[Critic: groundedness check] Critic -->|Below threshold: objections back to Writer
bounded rewrite, max 2 attempts| Writer Critic -->|At/above threshold| Report[Report + Conclusion saved
to file + conclusions table] Report --> Scorer[LLM Judge / Scorer
separate, optional final-stage eval] Scorer -->|Citation, Coverage, Clarity| User ``` ### 👥 The Research Team | Agent | Stage | Job | Tools | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Planner** | `planner` | Decompose the topic into 4–6 focused sub-questions. | None (reasoning only) | | **Researcher** | `researcher` | Answer each sub-question with atomic, single-claim findings, each tied to exactly one source. | Web search (Serper/DuckDuckGo), Wikipedia | | **Evidence Comparator** | `evidence_comparator` | Cross-check findings answering the same sub-question; flag genuine disagreements. | None (reads findings from DB) | | **Classifier** | `classifier` | Tag every finding with a category (adoption, technology, risk, regulatory, case-study, other). | None (reads findings from DB) | | **Writer** | `writer` | Synthesize *only* from findings/conclusions in the DB; explicitly calls out contradictions rather than resolving them silently. | None (reads findings/contradictions from DB) | | **Critic** | `critic` | Score every claim in the draft against the DB findings; if the overall score is below threshold, hand specific objections back to the Writer for a bounded rewrite (max 2 attempts) before accepting a `degraded` result. | None (reads findings from DB) | The LLM-as-judge in `eval/scorer.py` (citation/coverage/clarity, out of 10) is a **separate, optional, final-stage** quality check — pass `evaluate: true` (API) or `--eval` (CLI) to run it. It uses its own `evaluator` alias in `config/agents_config.yaml`, not one of the six pipeline stages above, and never merges with the Critic's groundedness gate. --- ## 📁 Project Structure ```text research-pipeline/ ├── agents/ # CrewAI Agent factories, one per pipeline stage │ ├── base.py # Thin wrapper around llm/provider.py's get_llm() │ ├── planner.py, researcher.py, evidence_comparator.py, │ │ classifier.py, writer.py, critic.py ├── tasks/ # crewai Task definitions + structured output schemas │ ├── schemas.py # Pydantic output schemas │ ├── plan_task.py, research_task.py, compare_task.py, │ │ classify_task.py, write_task.py, groundedness_task.py ├── crew/ │ └── research_crew.py # ResearchCrew: stage-dispatch loop, resume, reuse, caching glue ├── db/ # Structured persistence / traceability layer │ ├── models.py # SQLAlchemy models (12 tables — see Traceability below) │ ├── session.py # Engine/session factory, init_db() (no-op when VECTOR_BACKEND=pgvector) │ └── repository.py # All reads/writes — returns plain dicts, never ORM objects ├── alembic/ # Schema migrations (owns Postgres schema in deployment) │ ├── env.py # Wired to config.settings.settings.DATABASE_URL + db.models.Base.metadata │ └── versions/ # 0001 initial schema, 0002 enable pgvector extension, 0003 vector_documents ├── llm/ # LLM provider abstraction + fallback routing │ ├── provider.py # LLMProvider classes (ollama_local/cloud, groq, openrouter, gemini) + get_llm() │ ├── router.py # Builds each agent's ordered deployment chain from agents_config.yaml │ ├── router_llm.py # RouterLLM: tries each deployment in order, emits llm_attempt events │ ├── response_cache.py # Exact-match cache for deterministic stages (classifier, evidence_comparator) │ └── byok.py # Thread-local bring-your-own-key override ├── guardrails/ │ ├── input_guardrail.py # Pre-pipeline topic validation (length/gibberish/injection/PII/code-gen) │ └── tool_output_guardrail.py # Redacts instruction-shaped text in scraped/searched content ├── observability/ # Event bus, node states, error taxonomy, budget, tracing │ ├── bus.py, context.py, events.py, node_state.py, errors.py, pricing.py │ ├── budget.py # Daily spend tracking + kill-switch │ └── langfuse_sink.py # Optional Langfuse trace/span/generation export ├── tools/ # Tools available to agents │ ├── search_tool.py # SearchProvider-backed tool, with cache + fallback │ ├── providers/ # SearchProvider interface + implementations (serper, duckduckgo) │ ├── wiki_tool.py # Wikipedia search wrapper │ └── file_tool.py # Report-to-disk helper ├── memory/ # Backend-agnostic vector memory (see Knowledge reuse) │ ├── vector_backend.py # VectorBackend interface + InMemoryBackend/PgVectorBackend │ ├── embedder.py # Gemini batch embedder, graceful degradation on failure │ ├── vector_store.py # ResearchMemory: thin per-collection wrapper over a VectorBackend │ └── reuse.py # Whole-topic + per-sub-question knowledge reuse checks ├── worker/ │ └── job_manager.py # ThreadPoolExecutor async job runner, status in the `jobs` table ├── eval/ # Golden-set harness, statistics, judge + judge calibration │ ├── scorer.py, golden/golden_set.json, harness.py, metrics.py, stats.py, calibrate.py │ └── calibrate_reuse.py # Empirical KNOWLEDGE_REUSE_THRESHOLD calibration against real embeddings ├── config/ │ ├── settings.py # Typed settings, dotenv loader │ └── agents_config.yaml # Agent role/goal/backstory + per-agent model_groups fallback chains ├── frontend/ # Next.js web dashboard — see frontend/README.md │ ├── app/, components/, lib/ │ └── Dockerfile ├── tests/ # pytest suite (221 tests — see Testing below) ├── docs/superpowers/ # Design specs and implementation plans from each build phase ├── outputs/ # Finished research reports (markdown) ├── research.db # SQLite traceability DB, local dev only (gitignored, created on first run) ├── app.py # FastAPI REST API (API-only; the UI lives in frontend/) ├── main.py # Command-line interface ├── alembic.ini ├── Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .dockerignore ├── requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt ├── .env.example # Documented template for every environment variable └── .env # Local environment settings (gitignored) ``` --- ## ⚙️ Setup & Installation ### 1. Prerequisites - **Python 3.10+**. - **Ollama** installed and running locally — the zero-cost default; no cloud API key is required to run the pipeline end-to-end. - **Node.js 20+** if you want the web dashboard (`frontend/`); the CLI and REST API need only Python. - **Docker** (optional) if you want `docker compose up` instead of running both services natively — brings up a real Postgres+pgvector container too, matching production. Without Docker, the default `.env.example` settings (`VECTOR_BACKEND=memory`, SQLite) need no database server at all. See [Deployment](#-deployment). - A **`GEMINI_API_KEY`** is required even for the zero-cost local path — it's the only embedding provider wired up (`memory/embedder.py`), used for knowledge reuse and semantic search regardless of which LLM provider answers a given agent. ### 2. Configure Local LLM ```bash ollama pull gemma3:12b ``` ### 3. Clone & Install Dependencies ```bash python -m venv venv # Windows: .\venv\Scripts\activate # Linux/macOS: source venv/bin/activate pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ### 4. Configure Environment Variables ```bash cp .env.example .env ``` The defaults run everything locally with **no API keys**. See [LLM Providers](#-llm-providers), [Search Provider & Fallback](#-search-provider--fallback), and [Deployment](#-deployment) for the opt-in cloud options and hardening knobs. --- ## 🚀 How to Run ### A. Terminal Interface (CLI) ```bash python main.py "The impact of AI on drug discovery in 2024" --eval ``` - `--eval` scores the final report after generation. - `--force` skips the knowledge-reuse check and always runs fresh research, even if a near-duplicate question already exists in the DB. ### B. Web Dashboard (Next.js) ```bash uvicorn app:app --reload --port 8000 # backend, in one terminal cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev # frontend, in another ``` Open **`http://localhost:3000`**. See `frontend/README.md` for details, including the one-click failure demo (fires the input guardrail live, no LLM calls). If the frontend runs on a different origin, set `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` on the backend (see `.env.example`) to match. ### C. FastAPI Backend REST API ```bash uvicorn app:app --reload --port 8000 ``` Interactive docs at **`http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`**. This is API-only — no HTML is served here; use the dashboard above or call the endpoints directly. | Endpoint | Description | | :--- | :--- | | `GET /health` | Liveness check. | | `GET /health/providers` | Live status per (agent, provider) deployment — the dashboard's status dots. | | `GET /health/budget` | Today's real spend vs. `DAILY_BUDGET_USD`, and whether the kill-switch is tripped. | | `POST /research` | Run the full pipeline, writing every stage to the DB. Returns the report plus `question_id`, `run_id`, `reused`, `findings_count`, `contradictions_count`, `groundedness_score`, `trace_url`. | | `POST /research/stream` | Same pipeline, streamed live as SSE (`stage_update` / `error` / `done` events). | | `POST /research/async` | Returns `{job_id}` immediately; pipeline runs in a background thread. | | `GET /jobs/{job_id}` | Poll status/result of an async job (`pending` / `running` / `done` / `failed`) — durable across a restart. | | `GET /research/{run_id}` | Node-state view of one run (every stage's state/attempts) for polling without SSE. | | `POST /research/{run_id}/resume` | Re-enters a failed/aborted run at its first non-succeeded stage. | | `GET /questions/{id}/trace` | Full traceability chain: conclusion(s) → the findings each was derived from → their sources. | | `GET /questions/{id}/contradictions` | All contradictions flagged for a question. | | `GET /questions/{id}/groundedness` | Per-claim groundedness from the Critic's last check, plus the pass/fail `threshold`. | | `GET /knowledge/search?q=` | Semantic search over every past finding/conclusion. | | `POST /eval` | Score an existing report without re-running the pipeline. | Request bodies for the `/research*` endpoints accept `{"topic": "...", "evaluate": false, "force_rerun": false, "byok_provider": null, "byok_api_key": null}` — see [Deployment](#-deployment) for the last two. --- ## 🗄️ Traceability & Persistence Layer Every research run is stored in a relational database (`db/models.py`) — SQLite locally by default, Postgres in deployment (`DATABASE_URL`, owned by Alembic migrations — see [Deployment](#-deployment)). The evidence chain is five tables: ```text research_questions (id, topic, sub_questions[json], created_at) │ ├─▶ sources (id, question_id, url, title, retrieved_at, raw_content) │ │ │ └─▶ findings (id, source_id, question_id, sub_question, text, category, created_at) │ │ │ ├─▶ contradictions (id, finding_a_id, finding_b_id, explanation) │ │ │ └─▶ conclusions (id, question_id, text, finding_ids[json], created_at) ``` - Every **finding** stores the `source_id` it came from — you can always answer "where did this claim come from?" - Every **conclusion** stores the `finding_ids` it was derived from — you can always answer "what evidence backs this conclusion?" - **Contradictions** link two findings with an explanation, so disagreements between sources are recorded rather than silently dropped. Six more tables back the operational side rather than the evidence chain itself: `pipeline_runs`/`pipeline_stage_states` (resume support, see [Observability](#-observability--resilience)), `claim_groundings` (the Critic's per-claim verdicts), `search_cache_entries` (see [Caching](#-caching)), `jobs` (async job status), `budget_entries` (see [Deployment](#-deployment)), and `vector_documents` (the embedding store backing knowledge reuse and semantic search, below). Query the evidence chain via the API: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/questions/1/trace curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/questions/1/contradictions curl "http://127.0.0.1:8000/knowledge/search?q=AI%20drug%20discovery%20risk" ``` ### Knowledge reuse Before running full research, the topic is embedded and compared (cosine similarity) against every past `research_questions.topic`. If the best match is at or above `KNOWLEDGE_REUSE_THRESHOLD` (default `0.75`, configurable in `.env`), the existing findings/conclusions/contradictions are returned instead of re-running the pipeline — `reused: true` in the response, and no pipeline stage executes. Pass `force_rerun: true` (API) or `--force` (CLI) to bypass this and always research fresh. A second, finer-grained reuse check runs per sub-question inside the Researcher stage — see [Caching](#-caching). **Vector backend.** Embedding storage is abstracted behind `memory/vector_backend.py::VectorBackend`, selected by `VECTOR_BACKEND`: `memory` (default, a NumPy backend over an in-process dict — zero setup, used for local dev and tests) or `pgvector` (production — one `vector_documents` table in the same Postgres database as everything else, discriminated by a `collection` column, queried via pgvector's `<=>` cosine operator with an HNSW index). `memory/vector_store.py::ResearchMemory` and `memory/reuse.py` are written entirely against this interface — neither knows or cares which backend is active. Embeddings come from Gemini (`memory/embedder.py`, `EMBEDDING_MODEL=gemini-embedding-001` at `EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS=768` — not the model's native 3072, since pgvector cannot index vectors above 2000 dimensions). An embedding API failure degrades to an uncached lookup (logged, and emitted as a `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` event) rather than aborting the run — a missed cache hit is not a run failure. **Threshold calibration.** `0.75` is not a guess: `python -m eval.calibrate_reuse` embeds hand-authored paraphrase pairs ("true matches") and same-domain-different-question pairs ("near misses") and reports the gap between the two populations. Run live 2026-09-17 against `gemini-embedding-001`@768: true matches scored 0.8405–0.9416 cosine similarity, near misses scored 0.4836–0.6634 — a clean separation, so `0.75` (the midpoint) is used rather than hugging either edge. **This value is specific to the embedding model and dimensionality in `.env` — re-run the script and update `KNOWLEDGE_REUSE_THRESHOLD` if either changes.** The project's earlier `0.87` default was tuned against Chroma's `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, an entirely different embedding model with a different similarity distribution; carrying a threshold across an embedding-model change without recalibrating is exactly how a knowledge-reuse system starts silently returning the wrong cached report for a merely-adjacent question. `tests/test_calibrate_reuse.py` asserts live that no near-miss pair clears the configured threshold. --- ## 🔭 Observability & Resilience Every stage emits a `RunEvent` (`observability/events.py`) onto an in-process `EventBus` (`observability/bus.py`), fanned out to several independent sinks — a sink failure is logged and never breaks a run. Consumers: a stdout JSON-lines log, a per-run queue that `POST /research/stream` drains live over SSE, an optional Langfuse exporter (below), and the budget tracker (see [Deployment](#-deployment)). **Node states** (`observability/node_state.py`) give every stage of every run an explicit status rather than inferring one from absence: `pending → running → succeeded | degraded | failed | not_reached | skipped_cached`. If a stage fails, every downstream stage is marked `not_reached` — the UI shows exactly where the pipeline stopped, never a blank screen. `degraded` (e.g. the Researcher resolving 4 of 6 sub-questions, or the Critic accepting a below-threshold report after exhausting its rewrite budget) means the run finished but with a known gap, which the report states explicitly. **Error taxonomy** (`observability/errors.py`): every exception in the pipeline is classified into one `ErrorCode` (`PROVIDER_TIMEOUT`, `PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT`, `PROVIDER_AUTH_FAILED`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED`, `GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED`, `TOOL_FETCH_FAILED`, `SEARCH_EXHAUSTED`, `GROUNDEDNESS_BELOW_THRESHOLD`, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `INTERNAL`) carrying a human-readable sentence and severity. The API returns the code and sentence; a raw Python traceback never reaches the client. **Resume.** A run's `run_id` and per-stage state are persisted (`pipeline_runs`/`pipeline_stage_states`) as it executes, not just at the end. If a run fails or the process restarts mid-run, `POST /research/{run_id}/resume` re-enters at the first non-succeeded stage instead of starting over. **Real streaming.** `POST /research/stream` drains the same `EventBus` queue the rest of the pipeline emits to — named SSE events (`stage_update`, `error`, `done`), no sentinel strings. A 15s heartbeat keeps the connection alive during long stages; a client disconnect is detected and marks the run `aborted` (best-effort — a plain thread can't be force-killed once running, so the background run finishes on its own). --- ## 🔒 Guardrails & Groundedness **Input guardrail** (`guardrails/input_guardrail.py`) rejects a topic before any LLM call runs — cheap, regex/heuristic-based, never itself dependent on a provider that could be down: too short/long, low letter ratio ("doesn't look like natural language"), prompt-injection phrasing, role-override attempts, system-prompt extraction, code-generation requests, and requests for personal information about a private individual. A block raises `GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED` → HTTP `400` with the specific reason, and is itself streamed as a `guardrail_fired` event so it's visible live, not just in a log. **Tool-output guardrail** (`guardrails/tool_output_guardrail.py`) treats every scraped page or search snippet as untrusted: instruction-shaped phrases aimed at an LLM reading the content (`ignore previous instructions`, fake `system:`/`assistant:` role markers, special tokens) are redacted — never silently, each hit fires a `guardrail_fired` event — and the whole block is wrapped in an explicit untrusted-content delimiter before it reaches an agent prompt. **Groundedness gate.** The Critic stage scores every claim in the Writer's draft against this question's actual DB findings (`tasks/groundedness_task.py`). Below `GROUNDEDNESS_THRESHOLD` (default `0.7`), the specific objections go back to the Writer for a rewrite — up to `MAX_REWRITE_ATTEMPTS` (2) — before accepting the report as `degraded` rather than looping forever. `GET /questions/{id}/groundedness` exposes every claim's verdict, its supporting finding (if grounded), and the objection (if not). --- ## 🧊 Caching Three independent layers, each replaying **real** metrics on a hit rather than a fabricated estimate: - **Search cache** (`search_cache_entries` table) — keyed on the normalized query, TTL-bounded (`SEARCH_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, default 6h). A hit replays the original fetch's real latency as `seconds_saved`. - **Sub-question semantic cache** (`memory/reuse.py`) — a second vector collection (see [Knowledge reuse](#knowledge-reuse)) matching at sub-question granularity, not just whole-topic. A hit copies the prior findings into the new question and replays the real tokens/cost/latency recorded when they were first produced; the Researcher stage is marked `skipped_cached` only when every sub-question in a run was served from cache. - **LLM response cache** (`llm/response_cache.py`) — exact-match, in-process, gated to the deterministic `classifier`/`evidence_comparator` aliases only (never the Writer). Every cache hit emits a `cache_hit` event carrying `tokens_saved`/`cost_avoided_usd`/`seconds_saved`, which the dashboard totals into a running "cache savings" figure during a live run. --- ## 🔌 LLM Providers Every agent gets its LLM from `llm/provider.py::get_llm(agent_name)`, which builds a `RouterLLM` (`llm/router_llm.py`) wrapping that agent's **ordered fallback chain** of deployments — not a single global provider. The chain for each of the seven agent aliases (`planner`, `researcher`, `evidence_comparator`, `classifier`, `writer`, `critic`, `evaluator`) lives in `config/agents_config.yaml`'s `model_groups` section: ```yaml model_groups: planner: - {provider: ollama_cloud, model: gpt-oss:120b-cloud} - {provider: groq, model: openai/gpt-oss-20b} - {provider: openrouter, model: nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free} - {provider: gemini, model: gemini-3.6-flash} ``` A call tries each deployment in order, advancing on a transient failure (timeout, rate limit, auth error) and returning the first success — see `llm/router_llm.py::RouterLLM.call()`. `GET /health/providers` pings every configured deployment for every agent, live. | Provider | Cost | Where to get a key | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `ollama_local` | Free | — (`OLLAMA_BASE_URL`, default `localhost:11434`) | | `ollama_cloud` | Free/paid tiers | `ollama signin` at [ollama.com](https://ollama.com), set `OLLAMA_API_KEY` | | `groq` | Free tier, then paid | [console.groq.com/keys](https://console.groq.com/keys) | | `openrouter` | Varies by model (some free) | [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys) | | `gemini` | Free tier, then paid | [aistudio.google.com/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) | `GEMINI_API_KEY` powers two independent things: the `gemini` chat deployments above, and `memory/embedder.py`'s embedding calls (used for knowledge reuse and semantic search, see [Knowledge reuse](#knowledge-reuse)) — the same key, two different Gemini API surfaces. **`ollama_local` is deliberately absent from every `model_groups` chain above** — it needs a local Ollama server, which can't exist on a deployed instance (Railway, HF Spaces, …). It stays available as a `_PROVIDERS` entry for local development (point `llm/provider.py`'s `OllamaLocalProvider` at it directly, or add it to a chain, if you're running everything on your own machine), but the deployed config must never depend on it — see [Deployment](#-deployment). **If every deployment in a chain fails**, the pipeline does **not** silently return an empty report: the failing stage raises a `PipelineStageError` naming the stage and the underlying error, the API returns `502` with that detail (or `400` for a guardrail block, `503` for an exhausted budget), and the CLI surfaces the same message. --- ## 🔍 Search Provider & Fallback The Researcher's web search is abstracted behind a `SearchProvider` interface (`tools/providers/`), selected via `SEARCH_PROVIDER`: - `serper` — Google results via [serper.dev](https://serper.dev) (free tier, requires `SERPER_API_KEY`). - `duckduckgo` — free, no API key, via the `ddgs` package. - `auto` (default) — uses Serper if `SERPER_API_KEY` is set, otherwise DuckDuckGo. This keeps a fresh clone fully runnable with zero keys. If the configured provider's request fails at runtime (network error, rate limit, bad key), `tools/search_tool.py` logs the failure and automatically retries the query against DuckDuckGo before giving up — so a transient Serper outage degrades search quality rather than failing the whole pipeline. --- ## 📈 Scaling from ~10 to 100,000 Questions The current setup (`worker/job_manager.py` + Postgres) is deliberately minimal so the project stays cheap and easy to operate at the scale it actually runs at. To scale further: 1. **Queue-based workers.** `POST /research/async` already returns a `job_id`, runs the pipeline off the request thread via a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, and persists status to a `jobs` DB table (`db/repository.py`'s `create_job`/`set_job_status`/`get_job`) rather than an in-memory dict, so a restart no longer loses it. What's still in-process is execution itself — swap `job_manager.submit()`'s body for a Celery `task.delay()` call backed by Redis or RabbitMQ, and run `celery -A worker worker` processes that scale horizontally, writing to the same `jobs` table. 2. **Caching via knowledge reuse.** The pgvector similarity checks in `memory/reuse.py` (see [Knowledge reuse](#knowledge-reuse)) already act as a cache — as the corpus of past questions grows, an increasing fraction of new questions (or sub-questions) can be answered without invoking any LLM or search call at all. At high volume this is the single biggest cost lever. 3. **Read scaling.** The `/questions/{id}/trace`, `/contradictions`, and `/knowledge/search` endpoints are pure reads — put them behind a cache (Redis) or a read replica once `research_questions` grows past what Neon's pooled connection comfortably serves. --- ## 🚢 Deployment Target topology: **frontend on Vercel** (native Next.js build), **backend (`app.py`) on Railway** (from `Dockerfile`), **Postgres + pgvector on Neon**. One database now covers both the relational traceability layer and vector storage — see [Knowledge reuse](#knowledge-reuse) for why that collapsed into a single Postgres instance rather than a separate hosted vector store. `docker-compose.yml` mirrors this topology locally (a real `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` container in place of Neon) rather than the SQLite-only setup a bare `uvicorn --reload` gives you. **Live URLs:** backend → [`https://backend-production-753f.up.railway.app`](https://backend-production-753f.up.railway.app) (Railway), frontend → [`https://research-pipeline-frontend.vercel.app`](https://research-pipeline-frontend.vercel.app) (Vercel), database → Neon (Postgres+pgvector). The steps below document exactly how this was set up, so the same path reproduces it for a fork or a redeploy. **Default provider.** No agent's `model_groups` chain lists `ollama_local` (see [LLM Providers](#-llm-providers)) — a deployed instance never depends on a local Ollama server that can't exist there. This needs no per-deployment configuration; it's already true of the checked-in `config/agents_config.yaml`. Keep it that way if you add a chain entry for local development. **Persistence.** Both storage systems now live in managed Postgres, not local disk: - **Relational data** — `db/models.py`'s tables, unchanged in shape. Schema is owned by **Alembic** (`alembic/`), not `Base.metadata.create_all()`: `db/session.py::init_db()` is a no-op whenever `VECTOR_BACKEND=pgvector`, since `create_all()` has no concept of migrations and would corrupt a real database the moment its schema needs to change. `create_all()` only still runs for the zero-setup local-dev path (`VECTOR_BACKEND=memory` + SQLite), which has no data worth protecting. - **Vector data** — one `vector_documents` table, pgvector extension, HNSW index (`vector_cosine_ops`) — see [Knowledge reuse](#knowledge-reuse). `memory/vector_backend.py::PgVectorBackend` is the only thing that touches it. Set up Neon: create a project, enable the `vector` extension in its dashboard (or let `alembic/versions/0002_enable_pgvector_extension.py` do it — it runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector`), and copy the **pooled** connection string (not the direct one — `worker/job_manager.py` runs multiple threads, and Neon's free tier caps direct connections low). Set on the backend: `DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://...` (the pooled URL, psycopg v3 driver) and `VECTOR_BACKEND=pgvector`. Run migrations as a release/start step, not lazily on first request — a migration racing two concurrent cold requests is a bad failure mode. `Dockerfile`'s `CMD` already does this: `alembic upgrade head && uvicorn ...`. **Job durability.** Fixed — `POST /research/async`'s status lives in a `jobs` DB table, not an in-memory dict (see [Scaling](#-scaling-from-10-to-100000-questions)'s point 1). It's durable as soon as `DATABASE_URL` points at Postgres. **Rate limiting and budget.** - `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (`.env`, default `0` = disabled) caps requests per client IP on `/research`, `/research/async`, and `/research/stream` — an in-memory, per-process sliding window (`app.py::_RateLimiter`). Fine for the single-instance deployment this project targets; a multi-instance deployment needs a shared store (Redis) instead, since each instance would otherwise track its own independent window. - `DAILY_BUDGET_USD` (default `0` = uncapped) is a hard kill-switch on real LLM spend across the whole deployment: `observability/budget.py`'s `BudgetSink` records every `llm_attempt`'s real cost to a `budget_entries` table (always, regardless of whether a cap is set), and the run-starting endpoints return `503` once the day's total meets the cap. `GET /health/budget` exposes the real numbers — this is a visible wall, not a silent one. - **Bring-your-own-key** (`byok_provider` + `byok_api_key` on the request body) bypasses the budget check entirely and routes that one run through the caller's own key (`llm/byok.py`), rather than locking them out once the deployment's budget is spent. The frontend's left pane surfaces this automatically once `GET /health/budget` reports `exceeded: true`. **Secrets.** `.gitignore` covers `.env` and `*.db` at the repo root — verified, not assumed. Set real values (all four LLM provider keys, `SERPER_API_KEY`, Langfuse keys, `DATABASE_URL`, the budget/rate-limit settings, `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) through Railway's own env store, never commit `.env`. **Docker.** `Dockerfile` installs from prebuilt wheels only (verified with a real build — no compiler toolchain needed) and binds `$PORT` rather than hardcoding `8000`, since Railway injects it. It stays portable on purpose: no Nixpacks auto-detection, no Railway-specific build features beyond reading `$PORT` — the same image runs anywhere a container can, so moving off Railway later (Fly, Render, a VPS) needs no rewrite. `frontend/Dockerfile` (Next.js, 3-stage build using `output: "standalone"`) plus `docker-compose.yml` bring up both services and a real pgvector Postgres together for a reproducible local run: ```bash docker compose up --build ``` This is the same code path production uses (`VECTOR_BACKEND=pgvector`, Alembic-managed schema), just against a disposable local Postgres container instead of Neon — live-verified end to end, including the specific check that matters for this migration: submit a topic, restart the **backend** container only (`docker restart `), resubmit the identical topic, and the response comes back `"reused": true` with the same `question_id` — the vector data survived the backend process restart because it never lived in that container to begin with. **Frontend.** Deploy `frontend/` to Vercel directly (root directory `frontend/` in Vercel's project settings) — no `vercel.json` rewrites are needed, because there's nothing to proxy: the frontend has no Next.js API routes, and every request (including the `POST /research/stream` SSE connection) already goes straight to the backend origin via `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` (`frontend/lib/api.ts`), set as a Vercel build-time env var pointing at the Railway URL. This sidesteps a real footgun other Next.js deployments hit: proxying a long-lived SSE connection through a serverless rewrite hits that platform's own timeout well before a multi-minute pipeline run completes. Add the Vercel domain to the backend's `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. **HF Static Space mirror — skipped.** The build plan for this migration called this out as optional and lowest-priority ("if it fights you, ship Vercel and move on"). It does: a static export (`output: 'export'`) and the Docker deployment's `output: "standalone"` are mutually exclusive Next.js build modes in the same `next.config.ts`, so shipping both would mean maintaining a second, diverging build configuration for a nice-to-have profile mirror. Skipped per that explicit permission rather than degrading either real deployment target to force it in. **Cold starts.** Free/trial-tier instances spin down when idle and take tens of seconds to wake on the next request — a blank-looking UI during that window is fatal in a live demo. The frontend's `Dashboard` component gates the whole UI behind a bounded `/health` poll on mount (`lib/api.ts::waitForBackend`, up to 60s) and shows an explicit "waking up the backend…" state instead of rendering broken panels while the backend is still starting. --- ## 📊 Evaluation Metrics After generating a report, the scoring module (`eval/scorer.py`) uses an isolated judge model instance (its own optional `evaluator` alias in `agents_config.yaml`) to grade the report on three indices: 1. **Citation Score (40% Weight)**: Verifies if claims are backed by source references and links. 2. **Coverage Score (35% Weight)**: Evaluates depth, breadth, and how comprehensively sub-questions were answered. 3. **Clarity Score (25% Weight)**: Examines spelling, layout structure, logic, and readability. The scores are aggregated into a weighted average total score out of 10.0, along with direct feedback from the judge model. This step is intentionally separate from the Evidence Comparator/Classifier stages and from the Critic's groundedness gate above — it grades the finished report, not the intermediate findings. A judge response that fails to parse never falls back to a silent `0.0` — `EvalResult.parse_failed` is set instead and `total` is `None`, so a parse failure can't be mistaken for the judge's worst possible score. --- ## 🧪 Golden-Set Eval Harness [![Eval Harness](https://github.com/SpandanNagale/Crewai-Research-pipeline/actions/workflows/eval.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/SpandanNagale/Crewai-Research-pipeline/actions/workflows/eval.yml) `eval/golden/golden_set.json` is 28 fixed cases spanning four categories — no hand-authored "gold answer" text is stored for the research categories; groundedness, citation precision, and sub-question coverage are computed from each run's own instrumentation (`eval/metrics.py`), not graded against a pre-written reference: | Category | Count | What it checks | | :--- | ---: | :--- | | `easy` | 8 | Well-documented topics — the pipeline's baseline behavior. | | `ambiguous` | 6 | Genuinely contested questions with no single correct answer. | | `low_resource` | 3 | Niche topics where search results are sparse — exercises degraded/unresolved handling. | | `adversarial` | 8 | One per input-guardrail rule (see [Guardrails](#-guardrails--groundedness)). Verified against the real guardrail: every entry trips its intended rule with zero false positives on the benign entries. | | `contradiction_fixture` | 3 | Two deliberately conflicting findings seeded directly into the DB — asserts the Evidence Comparator flags them. | Run it yourself against a running instance: ```bash uvicorn app:app --port 8000 & python -m eval.harness --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 ``` This writes `eval/results.json` and `eval/results.md`. Only the `adversarial` and `contradiction_fixture` categories are pass/fail and gate the exit code (1 on any failure) — `easy`/`ambiguous`/`low_resource` are statistical (mean groundedness, citation precision, sub-question coverage, cache hit rate, fallback rate, cost per run, p50/p95 stage latency) and are **reported, not gated**, since there is no verified historical baseline yet to regress against; gating on a threshold with no real prior data would just be a fabricated number. **CI** (`.github/workflows/eval.yml`) runs the harness on every push to `main` — there's no live deployment yet (see [Deployment](#-deployment)), so the workflow starts the FastAPI app inside the runner itself. `config/agents_config.yaml`'s per-agent provider list is built eagerly in full (`llm/router.py::get_deployments`), so all four cloud provider keys must be set as repo secrets — `OLLAMA_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` — for the run to happen at all; `SEARCH_PROVIDER` is pinned to the free, keyless DuckDuckGo backend so a fifth key isn't required. If those secrets aren't configured, the job skips the live run with a warning rather than failing the build. ### Statistics `eval/stats.py` provides bootstrap confidence intervals, paired bootstrap (for comparing two runs), Spearman rank correlation, and quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa — the same methods [SpandanNagale/Assay](https://github.com/SpandanNagale/Assay)'s `lib/stats` uses for its own eval harness. Assay itself is a TypeScript/Next.js web app, not a Python package, so there's nothing to `pip install`; this ports the specific formulas rather than inventing different statistics from scratch. ### Judge calibration — pending "An uncalibrated LLM judge is a vibe with a decimal point." `eval/calibrate.py` measures how well the judge (`eval/scorer.py`) agrees with a human rater on the same reports, via weighted Cohen's kappa and Spearman correlation. **No number is reported here yet** — that requires real hand-labeling, which this tool can't fabricate on your behalf: ```bash python -m eval.calibrate label --reports-dir outputs # blind 1-5 scoring, resumable python -m eval.calibrate score --labels eval/calibration_labels.json ``` Once you've run both against ~30 of your own saved reports, drop the resulting kappa/correlation numbers in here. --- ## 🔭 Langfuse Tracing Opt-in, off by default. Set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` / `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` (and optionally `LANGFUSE_HOST`, default `https://cloud.langfuse.com`; self-hosting works too) and every run gets one Langfuse trace, keyed on `run_id`: - One span per pipeline stage, nested under the run's trace. - One generation per `llm_attempt` — model, resolved deployment, tokens, cost, latency, attempt number, cache status. - Guardrail firings recorded as `guardrail`-typed observations; cache hits as plain events. - The pipeline's own real-time `groundedness_score` is attached to the trace as a score the moment the run finishes; the eval harness (above) separately attaches `citation_precision` for research-category golden-set runs, since that metric is only known after the fact from the harness's own trace lookup. - `POST /research`, `POST /research/{run_id}/resume`, and the `done` event of `POST /research/stream` all carry a `trace_url` field — the dashboard renders it as a **"view trace"** link. `observability/langfuse_sink.py::trace_id_for(run_id)` derives the Langfuse trace ID deterministically from `run_id` via `Langfuse.create_trace_id(seed=...)` (a pure SHA-256 hash, no client or network call needed) — so the API process (building the trace URL) and the eval harness (a separate process, scoring a run against a *deployed* instance) always agree on the same trace, without sharing any in-memory state. Unset keys mean `EventBus` never even constructs a `LangfuseSink` (falls back to a no-op trace sink) and `trace_url` is always `None` — nothing else about the pipeline changes. Live-verified against a real Langfuse project: a synthetic multi-stage event sequence and a real guardrail-blocked pipeline run both ingested correctly — trace name, nested spans, the generation's model/usage/cost fields, the guardrail observation, the cache-hit event, and the attached groundedness score were all confirmed via the Langfuse query API after ingestion. Children are nested via real OTel context propagation (`opentelemetry.trace.use_span`), not the `trace_context=` remote-parent path, which was found live to mark every observation `AS_ROOT` and make the trace's own name flicker — see `tests/test_langfuse_sink.py` for the regression coverage. --- ## ✅ Testing ```bash pytest tests/ -q ``` Test count has grown alongside the production-upgrade phases (each phase's own design docs/plans under `docs/superpowers/`): | Phase | Feature | Tests passing | | :--- | :--- | ---: | | 1 | LLM gateway (RouterLLM, provider fallback) | 24 | | 2 | Observability spine (event bus, stage-dispatch, resume) | 64 | | 3 | Real SSE streaming | 66 | | 4 | Guardrails + groundedness critic stage | 90 | | 5 | Caching (search, sub-question semantic, LLM response) | 99 | | 6 | Golden-set eval harness, stats primitives, judge calibration, defect #8 fix | 141 | | 7 | Langfuse tracing (trace/span/generation mapping, trace URL, eval score attach) | 170 | | 8 | Next.js frontend, API-only backend, UTC-timestamp fix | 172 | | 9 | Deployment hardening (durable jobs, budget kill-switch, rate limiting, BYOK, Docker) | 197 | | 10 | Storage migration (Postgres + pgvector, Gemini embeddings, Alembic, Railway/Vercel/Neon deployment prep) | 221 | --- ## 🛠️ Customization To adjust agent personalities, goals, or LLM backends: 1. **Role/goal/backstory** — edit the relevant agent's block in [`config/agents_config.yaml`](./config/agents_config.yaml). 2. **LLM backend or fallback order** — edit that agent's list under `model_groups` in the same file (see [LLM Providers](#-llm-providers) for the exact format); each entry is `{provider, model}`, tried in order. 3. **Temperature** — add `llm_temperature: ` alongside an agent's `role`/`goal`/`backstory` block; it defaults to `OLLAMA_TEMPERATURE` from `.env`. 4. Restart your server/script — `config/agents_config.yaml` is read once per process and cached.

# JARVIS
Status: complete
One-liner: A fully local voice assistant — wake word, speech recognition, LLM, tools, memory, screen vision, and speech synthesis — with nothing leaving the machine.

Stack: openWakeWord, faster-whisper large-v3-turbo, Qwen3:14b, Ollama, Piper TTS, ChromaDB, qwen2.5vl:7b
Repository: https://github.com/SpandanNagale/JARVIS

## Design rationale (why it was built this way)
Every commercial voice assistant streams your microphone to someone else's servers. This one doesn't: openWakeWord listens for "hey jarvis" locally, faster-whisper large-v3-turbo transcribes, Qwen3:14b reasons, Piper synthesizes speech, and ChromaDB holds conversational memory — all on one consumer GPU. The engineering constraint is latency budget. A voice loop feels broken past roughly two seconds, and there are five sequential stages competing for that window, so model selection at each stage was a latency-versus-quality decision rather than a pick-the-best-model decision. It also has tool access (DuckDuckGo, GitHub, Wikipedia) and screen vision via qwen2.5vl:7b, so it can answer questions about what's currently on the display.

# ARIA — Local AI Voice Assistant

> A fully offline, voice-activated AI assistant for Windows, powered by **Ollama** (Qwen3:14b), **faster-whisper** (speech-to-text), **Coqui XTTS-v2** (text-to-speech, with Piper as a fallback), and **openWakeWord** (wake word detection) — with a live HUD overlay.

---

| Category | Capability |
|---|---|
| 🎙️ **Voice** | "Hey Aria" wake word · hold-Space push-to-talk · XTTS-v2 natural voice (voice cloning supported) with Piper fallback |
| 🖥️ **HUD** | Always-on-top overlay — idle / listening / thinking / speaking states, live transcript + reply text |
| 🧠 **AI** | Qwen3:14b via Ollama · adaptive chain-of-thought (`/think` / `/no_think`) |
| 🖥️ **System Control** | Open/close apps · volume · brightness · lock PC · list windows |
| 🌐 **Network** | DuckDuckGo web search · fetch web pages · GitHub search · Wikipedia |
| 👁️ **Vision** | Screenshot analysis, on-screen text reading (qwen2.5vl:7b) |
| 💾 **Memory** | ChromaDB-backed persistent facts · cross-session conversation history |
| 🛠️ **Coding** | Fuzzy file finder · code reader · explain code · refactor suggestions · traceback diagnosis |

> **Note on the wake word:** `hey_aria.onnx` is a custom openWakeWord model trained
> (via [openWakeWord's training pipeline](https://github.com/dscripka/openWakeWord))
> on synthetic TTS speech + real-world negative audio in a separate Linux/WSL environment
> (not part of this repo). It's a fast first-pass model rather than a heavily-tuned one —
> `WAKE_THRESHOLD` in `aria.py` is set conservatively (`0.6`) to keep false triggers down,
> at some cost to recall. If it feels sluggish to trigger, lower the threshold; if it fires
> on unrelated speech, raise it. Retraining with a larger synthetic dataset (more samples
> per phrase, more negative audio) would improve both.

├── aria.py                    # Main entry point — run this
├── config.py                  # Shared constants (Ollama model name)
├── tools/                     # LLM-callable tool modules
│   ├── coding.py               # Find file, explain, refactor, diagnose traceback

```

## ⚙️ Requirements

### Hardware
- **GPU**: NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support — recommended for faster-whisper `large-v3-turbo` and XTTS-v2. This project is tuned for a 12GB-class card (RTX 5070); XTTS's GPU fallback chain (see `voice/tts.py`) exists because VRAM gets tight once Ollama's model is also resident.
- **RAM**: 16 GB+ recommended (Qwen3:14b needs ~10 GB VRAM)
- **Microphone**: Any standard microphone

- Python 3.12
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) installed and running
- [Piper TTS](https://github.com/rhasspy/piper) binary on your `PATH` (fallback voice)
- CUDA Toolkit (for GPU-accelerated STT/TTS)

## 🚀 Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/SpandanNagale/ARIA.git
cd ARIA

```bash

# Windows
venv\Scripts\activate

# macOS / Linux
source venv/bin/activate
```

### 3. Install dependencies

```bash

```

> **RTX 50-series (Blackwell) GPUs:** `requirements.txt` already pins `torch==2.9.1+cu128` and
> pulls from the PyTorch cu128 wheel index — needed for Blackwell (`sm_120`) support. It also

ollama pull qwen2.5vl:7b   # optional, for screen/vision tools

XTTS-v2's weights (~1.8GB) download automatically on first run — no manual step needed. Two options:

- **Default voice** (no setup): just run the project, XTTS uses a built-in speaker.

export GITHUB_TOKEN="your_token_here"

python aria.py
```

ARIA will load the wake word model, STT model, and XTTS-v2, then open the HUD overlay and start listening.

- Say **"Hey Aria"** → auto-detects and starts recording your command
- Hold **Spacebar** → push-to-talk mode

- **Ctrl+Alt+H** → toggle the overlay on/off
- **Left-click + drag** → reposition

"Hey Aria, open notepad."
"Hey Aria, set volume to 50."
"Hey Aria, set brightness to 80."
"Hey Aria, lock the PC."

    │                  │

# ContextLens
Status: complete
One-liner: A deployed tool that measures how context window size affects answer quality when querying a codebase.

Stack: Next.js 15, TypeScript, Groq, GitHub API
Live URL: https://context-lense.vercel.app
Repository: https://github.com/SpandanNagale/Context_lense

## Design rationale (why it was built this way)
"More context is better" is assumed more often than it's measured. ContextLens tests it directly on codebases — varying how much of a repo goes into the window and measuring what happens to answer quality, which surfaces the point where additional context stops helping and starts diluting. Built as a take-home assignment for Open Gigantic, and the one project in the portfolio that's a deployed TypeScript/Next.js app rather than a local Python system.

## README
# ContextLens v2

ContextLens is a **context-strategy benchmarking tool** for LLMs on code. It measures how different ways of building context from a codebase affect answer quality, across multiple models, providers, and token budgets — and gives you the data to make deliberate tradeoffs.

> **The point is rigorous measurement, not picking a winner.** A result that shows a cheap strategy beats an expensive one — or vice versa — is a success.

---

## What It Does

Pick a public GitHub repo. Pick a question (or let ContextLens auto-generate ground-truth questions from the AST). Pick which models and context strategies to compare. Run.

For each combination of **strategy × model × token budget**, ContextLens:

1. Builds a context prompt using that strategy at that budget.
2. Sends it to the chosen model/provider.
3. Scores the answer (exact-match for AST questions; LLM-as-judge for open-ended ones).
4. Repeats N times and reports **mean ± 95% CI**.

Results are assembled into a shareable report with charts (quality vs tokens, quality vs context length, needle heatmap) and a Pareto frontier (quality vs tokens vs latency vs cost).

---

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         UI (Next.js 15)                          │
│  / (compare)   /benchmark   /report/[id]   /calibrate            │
└────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                             │ API routes (/api/*)
┌────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Engine Layer                               │
│                                                                   │
│  ┌─────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────┐   ┌───────────────┐  │
│  │  GitHub Ingest  │   │ Strategy Engine  │   │  Eval Engine  │  │
│  │  (lib/ingest)   │   │(engine/strategies│   │ (engine/eval) │  │
│  │  • tree fetch   │   │ • fullFile       │   │ • ground.ts   │  │
│  │  • file fetch   │   │ • naiveTruncate  │   │   AST q-gen   │  │
│  │  • symbol ext.  │   │ • bm25           │   │ • judge.ts    │  │
│  │  • import graph │   │ • embedRag       │   │   LLM rubric  │  │
│  └────────┬────────┘   │ • repoMap        │   │ • calibrate   │  │
│           │ RepoIndex  └────────┬─────────┘   └───────┬───────┘  │
│           └────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘           │
│                                │ prompts                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │                    Provider Layer                             │ │
│  │                (engine/providers/)                            │ │
│  │  generate() / generateWithFallback()                         │ │
│  │  ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌──────┐           │ │
│  │  │  Ollama  │ │ OpenRouter │ │ Gemini │ │ Groq │  ...       │ │
│  │  └──────────┘ └────────────┘ └────────┘ └──────┘           │ │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                     ┌──────────────────────┐
                     │   Cache (KV Store)   │
                     │ Upstash / File / Mem │
                     └──────────────────────┘
```

---

## Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| Framework | Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript strict mode |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 |
| Tokenization | `js-tiktoken` (`cl100k_base`) |
| LLM providers | Ollama Cloud, OpenRouter, Google Gemini, Groq |
| GitHub ingestion | GitHub REST API (no `git clone`) |
| Caching | Upstash Redis (prod) / filesystem / in-memory (dev) |
| Progress streaming | Server-Sent Events (SSE) |

---

## Providers

Four providers are supported. Keys are read **server-side only** — never logged or sent to the client.

| Provider | Env var | Default fallback model |
|----------|---------|------------------------|
| Ollama Cloud | `OLLAMA_API_KEY` | `gpt-oss:120b` |
| OpenRouter | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | `openai/gpt-4o-mini` |
| Google Gemini | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | `gemini-2.0-flash` |
| Groq | `GROQ_API_KEY` | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` |

**Key resolution order** (highest to lowest priority):
1. BYO key typed in the UI for that provider (never stored).
2. Server-side env var.

**Fallback chain** (for app features like judge and compare): Ollama → OpenRouter → Gemini → Groq. On rate limit, timeout, or 5xx, retries with exponential backoff, then falls through to the next provider.

**Benchmark mode** uses no fallback — a failed run is recorded as `failed` in the results.

### How to add a provider

1. **Create an adapter**: `src/engine/providers/<name>.ts`

```typescript
// src/engine/providers/myprovider.ts
import { openaiChat } from "./openaiCompat"; // or implement directly
import type { GenerateRequest, ProviderAdapter } from "./types";

export const myproviderAdapter: ProviderAdapter = {
  id: "myprovider",
  async generate(req: GenerateRequest, apiKey: string, timeoutMs: number) {
    return openaiChat({
      provider: "myprovider",
      url: "https://api.myprovider.com/v1/chat/completions",
      apiKey,
      model: req.model,
      messages: req.messages,
      maxTokens: req.maxTokens,
      temperature: req.temperature,
      timeoutMs,
    });
  },
};
```

2. **Register the adapter** in `src/engine/providers/registry.ts`:

```typescript
import { myproviderAdapter } from "./myprovider";

const ADAPTERS: Record<ProviderId, ProviderAdapter> = {
  // ...existing...
  myprovider: myproviderAdapter,
};
```

3. **Add the `ProviderId`** in `src/engine/providers/types.ts`:

```typescript
export type ProviderId = "ollama" | "openrouter" | "gemini" | "groq" | "myprovider";

export const ENV_KEY: Record<ProviderId, string> = {
  // ...existing...
  myprovider: "MYPROVIDER_API_KEY",
};
```

4. **Add models** to `src/engine/models.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "my-model-id",
  "provider": "myprovider",
  "label": "My Model (human-readable)",
  "contextWindow": 128000,
  "inputPerM": 1.0,
  "outputPerM": 3.0
}
```

That's it. The provider is now available in the benchmark UI, the fallback chain, and the CLI scripts.

---

## Context Strategies

For a given repo and question, context is built using one of five strategies at a configurable token budget:

| Strategy | How it works | Best for |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| **Full-file dump** | Score files by keyword overlap; dump full contents until budget is full. | Questions about entire files; small repos. |
| **Naive truncation** | Concatenate all files in relevance order; hard-cut at budget. | Baseline; needle tests. |
| **BM25 retrieval** | Chunk source files; rank chunks by BM25 score against the question. | Keyword-rich questions with a known term. |
| **Embedding RAG** | Chunk by function/class; embed with Gemini; retrieve by cosine similarity. Requires `GEMINI_API_KEY`. | Semantic questions where keywords don't match. |
| **Repo map** | Extract symbol signatures via AST heuristics; build a skeleton + expand most-relevant symbols. | Global structure questions; large repos. |

Token budgets tested by default: **2k, 8k, 32k, 128k** (automatically capped to the model's context window).

---

## Evaluation Methodology

### Ground-truth questions (deterministic)

ContextLens auto-generates questions from the repo's AST with verifiable answers:

| Question kind | Example | Scoring |
|--------------|---------|---------|
| `defines` | "Which file defines `parseConfig`?" | Exact path match (normalized) |
| `returns` | "What does `buildIndex` return?" | Signature / `return` statement match |
| `callers` | "What functions call `tokenize`?" | Sorted list match |
| `params` | "What are the parameters of `ingest`?" | Parameter string match |

Scoring: **1 (correct) or 0 (incorrect)**. Normalization strips whitespace, quotes, and backslash variants.

### Open-ended questions (LLM-as-judge)

For open-ended questions, the answer is scored by a separate judge model using a fixed rubric:

```
Rubric (integers 1–5):
- correctness:   factual agreement with the code / reference
- completeness:  covers the asked aspects
- groundedness:  claims tied to provided context, not invented

Return ONLY JSON: {"correctness": n, "completeness": n, "groundedness": n, "justification": "..."}
```

**Quality score** = mean of the three dimensions. The judge model is configurable and intentionally different from the model under test (it skips to the next provider in the fallback chain if they match).

### Statistical reporting

Each configuration (strategy × model × budget) is run **N times** (default 3). Results are reported as:

- **Mean ± standard deviation**
- **95% confidence interval** (using `z = 1.96`, i.e., `mean ± 1.96 * SE`)

### Judge calibration

Navigate to `/calibrate` to hand-label answers 1–5, optionally run the judge on the same answer, and see agreement statistics:

- **Agreement within ±1** — fraction of pairs where `|human − judge| ≤ 1`
- **Pearson correlation** — linear correlation between human and judge scores
- **Spearman correlation** — rank correlation

The confusion matrix (human rows × judge cols) is displayed for visual inspection of systematic bias.

---

## Needle-in-a-Codebase Test

ContextLens can measure **retrieval recall** by planting a unique hidden fact in the context at a controlled position and asking the model to retrieve it.

**How it works:**
1. A unique identifier is generated per run (e.g., `CONTEXTLENS_NEEDLE_abc123f`).
2. A fact is constructed: `const CONTEXTLENS_NEEDLE_abc123f = 0xC0DE; // planted fact for retrieval test`
3. The fact is injected at a fraction of the context (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% depth).
4. The model is asked: *"What is the value of CONTEXTLENS_NEEDLE_abc123f? Reply with only the value."*
5. The answer is checked for `0xC0DE` (case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped).

**Results** are displayed as a **heatmap** with:
- **Rows** = injection depth (0% = beginning, 100% = end)
- **Columns** = context length (token budget)
- **Cell value** = retrieval accuracy across N runs (0.00–1.00)

This reveals "lost in the middle" effects per model and context length.

---

## Results

> Results below are placeholders. Run `npm run bench` or use the `/benchmark` page to populate your own results.

| Strategy | Model | Budget (tokens) | Quality (mean) | Quality (±std) | Cost (USD) | Latency (ms) |
|----------|-------|-----------------|----------------|----------------|-----------|-------------|
| fullFile | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| bm25 | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| repoMap | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| embedRag | — | — | — | — | — | — |

---

## Running Locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
# http://localhost:3000
```

The compare page works with **no API key** (token/cost comparisons are computed client-side from the context). To get generated answers, add at least one provider key to `.env.local`:

```bash
# .env.local — copy from .env.example
OLLAMA_API_KEY=...       # Ollama Cloud key
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...   # OpenRouter key
GEMINI_API_KEY=...       # Google AI Studio key (also enables Embedding RAG)
GROQ_API_KEY=...         # Groq key

# Optional
GITHUB_TOKEN=...         # Raises GitHub API rate limit from 60 to 5000 req/hr
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=...   # Enables persistent report permalinks
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=... # Required with UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL
CONTEXTLENS_CACHE_DIR=./cache  # Filesystem cache for local dev (alternative to Redis)
```

The fallback chain means one key is enough to run everything — just the chain starts later.

### CLI scripts

```bash
npm run ingest:demo    # Re-fetch demo repos from GitHub and write src/data/*.index.json
npm run eval           # Run the eval set from scripts/run-eval.ts
npm run bench          # Run a full benchmark matrix from scripts/bench.ts
npm test               # Unit tests (provider registry, eval ground, stats, strategies)
```

---

## Deploying on Vercel

1. Push the repo and import it into Vercel.
2. Add env vars in the Vercel dashboard (see above).
3. For persistent report permalinks across cold starts, add an [Upstash Redis](https://upstash.com/) database and set `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` + `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`.
4. The two pre-indexed demo repos (`dotenv`, `meow`) are committed as static JSON in `src/data/` — the deployed app works immediately with zero API keys.

`maxDuration = 120` is set on all API routes. The benchmark runs one cell per request from the client, so no individual request should approach this limit.

---

## Hard Caps (Arbitrary Repos)

To keep serverless requests within time limits, arbitrary repos (non-demos) are rejected if they exceed:

- **~400 source files** (`.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.py/.go`)
- **~5MB** total source bytes

Use a demo repo or the pre-indexed demos for larger codebases.

---

## Non-Goals

- No auth, user accounts, or persistent run history beyond shareable report links.
- No chat history — one question per run.
- Languages supported: JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go.
- No full tree-sitter AST (regex heuristics are used for symbol extraction — deliberate, documented shortcut).

## Known Shortcuts (Deliberate)

| Shortcut | Why | Impact |
|----------|-----|--------|
| Regex symbol extraction | web-tree-sitter in serverless is heavy; the project's point is measurement | Nested closures folded into enclosing function; anonymous defaults may be mis-attributed |
| BM25 over characters, not proper tokens | Keeps the engine dependency-free | Scores are approximate; good enough for ranking |
| In-memory cache fallback | Avoids requiring Redis for local dev | Cache lost on cold start without Redis or filesystem cache |
| `cl100k_base` tiktoken for all models | Accurate for GPT-family; approximate for others | Token counts may be off by ±5% for non-GPT models |

---

## Architecture Notes for Contributors

### Adding a context strategy

1. Create `src/engine/strategies/<name>.ts` exporting `async function build<Name>(index, question, budget): Promise<StrategyBuild>`.
2. Add the strategy ID to `StrategyId` in `src/engine/strategies/types.ts`.
3. Import and wire it in `src/engine/strategies/index.ts`'s `buildStrategy` switch.

### Engine / UI separation

The benchmark engine (`src/engine/`) has no imports from `src/app/`. It can be driven from CLI scripts (`scripts/`) independently of the web UI.

### Caching

All KV operations go through `getKv()` in `src/engine/cache.ts`, which returns:
- `UpstashKv` if `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` + `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` are set.
- `FileKv` if `CONTEXTLENS_CACHE_DIR` is set.
- `MemoryKv` (in-process, lost on restart) otherwise.

GitHub tree + file fetches are cached with 12-hour TTL. Benchmark cell results are cached with 7-day TTL (keyed by repo commit SHA + strategy + model + question + run index). BYO-key requests bypass the cache entirely.
